Objective Type Test Shorthand (English) Test Typing Speed Test on Computer Interview

pattern_table.Subject / Details: General English (25), General Knowledge (25), Judiciary provisions in Constitution of India (25), Supreme Court Rules, 2013 (15), Knowledge of Computer operation (10)
English Shorthand Test at 120 w.p.m. (Transcription time: 45 minutes; 7 minutes dictation)
Typing Speed Test on Computer in English with minimum speed of 40 w.p.m.

exam_pattern.details: Minimum Qualifying Marks: 50 marks for Objective Type Test (out of 100); 50 marks for Shorthand Test (out of 100); 10 marks for Computer Typing Test (out of 20); 15 marks for Interview (out of 30). | Negative Marking: There will be no negative marking in the Objective Type Test.

how_to_apply: Visit the official website of the Supreme Court of India at www.sci.gov.in and access the recruitment link.
Register online and fill out the application form with all required personal and academic details.
Upload scanned copies of your recent photograph, signature, Class Xth, Class XIIth and Graduation certificates, experience certificate, and caste/community certificate (if applicable).
Preview the filled application form carefully and complete final submission since modifications are not permitted once submitted.
Pay the non-refundable application fee online through the UCO Bank payment gateway.
Retain your application number and take a printout of the filled application form for your records and future reference.
important_instructions: All admissions to tests and interviews are provisional, and eligibility documents will be verified during document verification. Candidates must retain their application number carefully to download admit cards from the official website. No admit cards will be sent by post. No TA/DA will be payable for appearing in tests or the interview. Candidates working in Central/State Government Departments, Nationalized Banks, or PSUs must submit a No Objection Certificate during document verification. Selected candidates may be required to work even at odd hours and holidays and must submit an undertaking to that effect. Submitting more than one application form will result in only the last submitted form being considered.

faq.question: Q1. What is the start date to apply for Supreme Court of India Court Master (Shorthand) Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The online registration for application starts on 25th October, 2026.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to submit the online application form?
faq.answer: The last date for submission of application is 15th November, 2026, up to 11.55 p.m.

faq.question: Q3. How many vacancies are announced in this recruitment?
faq.answer: There are 20 tentative vacancies for the Court Master (Shorthand) post.

faq.question: Q4. What is the required educational qualification?
faq.answer: Candidates must possess a Bachelor's degree from a recognized University in India, proficiency in Shorthand at 120 w.p.m. in English, and computer operation knowledge with a typing speed of 40 w.p.m.

faq.question: Q5. What is the age limit for applicants?
faq.answer: Candidates should not be below 30 years of age and the upper age limit is 45 years as on 1st October, 2026, with relaxations as per rules.

faq.question: Q6. What is the application fee for General category candidates?
faq.answer: The non-refundable application fee for General/Unreserved category candidates is Rs. 1,500/- plus Bank charges.

faq.question: Q7. What is the salary offered for the Court Master (Shorthand) post?
faq.answer: The post is placed in Level 11 of Pay Matrix (Rs. 67,700 - Rs. 2,08,700/-) with initial Basic Pay of Rs. 67,700/- plus allowances.

faq.question: Q8. Is there any negative marking in the Objective Type Test?
faq.answer: No, there will be no negative marking in the Objective Type Test.

faq.question: Q9. Where should candidates send notifications if they get employed after submitting the application?
faq.answer: Candidates must intimate employment status to the Branch Officer, Recruitment Cell, via email at [email protected] without fail.

faq.question: Q10. Will admit cards be sent by post?
faq.answer: No, admit cards will not be sent by post and must be downloaded from the website of the Supreme Court of India.
